paper.title: llama.cpp v1.1.0
paper.abstract: Overview llama.cpp v1.1.0 adds the Inkling 2 family (base, Mini and DSpark), Domyn Edge 4B, Zaya1 8B, RAON-1-mini and Hy4 flash, splits DFlash speculative decoding into separate draft methods, and deprecates the old llama_batch API in favour of llama_batch_ext . It brings a large set of TTS and audio models (Kokoro, Zonos3-Mini, tiny-voca, VoxCPM2, MiniMax-Music3, YuE2, Fish S2, Higgs v3/VibeVoice-ASR and Kyutai Hibiki), token-aware chat parsing, named tool choice, automatic per-tensor quantization targeting a bpw or size budget, a slot-scheduling refactor in llama-server , a redesigned Llama Chat web UI with voice messages and agent traces, and updates ggml to v1.1.1. and manage MCP from Settings ( #33036 ) stop the streaming reply with Escape and make npx llama-chat default to :9931 ( #33051 , #33095 ) ggml changes v1.1.0 : ggml v1.1.0 extends the graph API for new model families, strengthens scheduler and backend behavior, and brings broad performance work across all backends. The API gains gated-delta-net replay, flash-attention indexed bias, ordered asynchronous host input copies, and scheduler scratch reservation, plus new SLEEP and SIGMOID_BACK operators. Core adds BF16 coverage for more operations, faster quantization and math helpers, and new CPU quant kernels, while backends add stream-k matmul, chunked command buffers, NVFP4, CONV_2D acceleration, wider FP8/BF16 support, and many tuning and correctness fixes. v1.1.1 : ggml v1.1.1 lands Hexagon 2.0 with INT-HMX W8A8 matmul, automatic F32 to F16 lowering and generic DMA pipelines, and brings a CUDA FlashAttention data-loading refactor, a SYCL gated-delta-net ESIMD kernel with fused recurrent convolutions, small-K Metal mat-vec tuning, and a WebGPU log1p for softplus. It also adds the TANH backward pass, OpenVINO decode and op-test fixes, and 16-head lightning-indexer support on CUDA. paper.title: b12764: metal : spread the short mat-vec lanes over src1 rows (#33034)
paper.abstract: metal : spread the short mat-vec lanes over src1 rows The short mat-vec kernel (K < 32) mapped its 32 lanes to 32 src0 rows and handled one src1 row per threadgroup, so with few src0 rows most lanes were idle. It now covers min(ne01, 32) src0 rows of 32/that src1 rows. This is the weighted sum over the depth states of Inkling 2 since #32855 (1-3 src0 rows, K = number of states, 2304 src1 rows). Inkling-2-Mini UD-Q4_K_XL, M5 Max, master -> this PR: pp512 888 -> 1052 t/s, pp2048 771 -> 894 t/s, tg128 unchanged. PPL and greedy output bit-identical, the graph is unchanged. Tested: test-backend-ops -b MTL0 -o MUL_MAT (new small-K cases). cont : clean-up comment Co-authored-by: Georgi Gerganov ggerganov@gmail.com

paper.title: Release: v5.21.0
paper.abstract: Release v5.21.0 New Model additions MiniCPM-OCR MiniCPM-OCR is a document-understanding model from OpenBMB's MiniCPM-V family. It keeps the MiniCPM-V 4.6 architecture, which pairs a SigLIP vision encoder and a window-attention merger with a Qwen3.5 language model. It is specialized for reading text-dense images such as scanned pages, screenshots, receipts and tables. Links: Documentation | Paper Feat test ( #49920 ) by @guarin in #49920 Flint Flint is Recursive's mixture-of-experts language model. Compared to a standard SwiGLU MoE transformer such as Qwen3-MoE, it uses hybrid attention (sliding-window attention with rotary embeddings over the current token and the previous 512 tokens in most layers, and full attention without positional encoding in the remaining layers). It also has learned attention sinks, as in GPT-OSS, with per-head RMS-normalized queries and keys. Each sparse layer routes a token to 6 of 256 experts by sigmoid score and adds an ungated shared expert, and the first two layers are dense. Links: Documentation Add Flint model support. ( #49824 ) by @lovishmadaan in #49824 UltraVBert UltraVBert extends ModernVBert by pairing the UltraBERT text encoder with a SigLIP vision encoder for visual document understanding and retrieval. Its image processor splits each page into 512-pixel tiles plus a global view. The connector merges each 4 x 4 block of vision patches into one token, so a tile becomes 64 image tokens, and RMS-normalizes them to the scale of UltraBERT's token embeddings. The max_image_tiles setting (27 by default) caps the number of tiles per page. Links: Documentation Add UltraVBERT ( #49685 ) by @athrael-soju in #49685 Gradium Phonon TTS Gradium Phonon TTS is Gradium's family of on-device text-to-speech models, trained with the Pocket TTS recipe. A causal transformer reads a voice prompt and the text, then emits one continuous 32-dimensional audio latent per step at 12.5 Hz through a one-step flow head, and an end-of-speech head decides when the utterance ends. The latents are decoded to 24 kHz audio by a Pocket TTS audio tokenizer. Unlike Pocket TTS, voice conditioning uses 512-dimensional latents from a separate, unreleased speaker codec, so voices come as precomputed latents and cannot be cloned from a recording.
